title: Superintelligence_ban
summary:
A superintelligence ban refers to proposed legal, ethical, or policy measures intended to restrict or prohibit the development of artificial superintelligence, AI systems that would surpass human cognitive abilities in nearly all domains. The idea arises from concerns that such systems could become uncontrollable, potentially posing existential threats to humanity or causing severe social and economic disruption.

The concept of limiting or banning superintelligence research has roots in early 21st-century debates on artificial general intelligence safety. Thinkers such as Nick Bostrom and Eliezer Yudkowsky warned that self-improving AI could rapidly exceed human oversight. Supporters argue that once AI systems surpass human intelligence, traditional containment, alignment, and control methods may fail, and that even limited experimentation could lead to irreversible outcomes. Some propose international treaties modeled after the nuclear non-proliferation framework to prevent a competitive AI arms race.

Opponents argue that a ban would be difficult to define and enforce, given the lack of a precise threshold distinguishing advanced AGI from superintelligence, and warn that excessive restriction could slow scientific progress, hinder beneficial automation, and encourage unregulated underground research. Although no government has enacted an explicit superintelligence ban, the idea has been debated within the European Union, United Nations, and several independent AI safety organizations.

In October 2025, an open letter calling for prohibition of superintelligent AI development was signed by over 850 people including tech leaders Richard Branson and Steve Wozniak, and AI pioneers Yoshua Bengio and Geoff Hinton. The statement called for a prohibition not to be lifted before broad scientific consensus on safety and strong public buy-in. Polling showed 64% of Americans believe superintelligence should not be developed until provably safe, and only 5% believe it should be developed as quickly as possible.
